part.text:
Fixed. The root cause of the #3215 compilation failure ("cannot select from a type variable" / "constructor B(...) is undefined"): when a `@SuperBuilder` child class extends a parent whose name collides with the builder's generated type parameter `B` (e.g. `class A extends B`), the generated child builder `ABuilder<C, B>` shadowed the class `B`, breaking the `extends B.BBuilder<C, B>` reference.

**Fix** — in both `src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleSuperBuilder.java` and `src/core/lombok/eclipse/handlers/HandleSuperBuilder.java`, `gatherUsedTypeNames` now also collects the first token of every type name appearing in the annotated class's `extends`/`implements` clauses, so `generateNonclashingNameFor` picks `B2`/`B4` etc. instead of a shadowing name.

**Validation** (in the container):
- `ant test.instance` (delombok suite): 379 tests, 0 failures — `javac-SuperBuilderNameClashes` now passes (previously the only failure)
- `ant test.javacCurrent`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- `ant test.ecj11`: all 312 tests pass — `ecj-SuperBuilderNameClashes` passes
- The issue's exact `A extends B` reproduction compiles cleanly with the built agent
